content.text: The updater gyrokinetic/zero/gk_collisionless_flux.c computes the collisionless gyrokinetic flux at cell surfaces in our DG scheme. It has a while loop over cells and within it a for loop over directions. Within that for loop it computes the flux for interior cell surfaces, and it has a special case ("idx[dir] == phase_range->upper[dir]") for the upper cell so it computes the upper domain surface flux. Can you change this so that there are special cases at both the lower and upper domain surfaces please? just modify the .c file for now, we will add the new Maxima-generated kernels into gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_priv.h and modify the CUDA version at a subsequent stage.

The updater gyrokinetic/zero/gk_collisionless_flux.c computes the collisionless gyrokinetic flux at cell surfaces in
  our DG scheme. It has a while loop over cells and within it a for loop over directions. Within that for loop it
  computes the flux for interior cell surfaces, and it has a special case ("idx[dir] == phase_range->upper[dir]") for
  the upper cell so it computes the upper domain surface flux. Can you change this so that there are special cases at
  both the lower and upper domain surfaces please? You may need to need to modify gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_priv.h to
  add the new Maxima-generated kernels; i've only generated the 1x2v ones as examples,
  gyrokinetic/ker/gk_collisionless_flux/gk_collisionless_flux_surfx_1x2v_ser_p1.c and
  gyrokinetic/ker/gk_collisionless_flux/gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_1x2v_ser_p1.c. And we will modify the CUDA
  version at a subsequent stage when we've finalized the C version.

312	choose_gk_collisionless_flux_surf_conf_kern(int dir, int cdim, int vdim, int poly_order, enum gkyl_gyrokinetic_bc_type bc)
313	{
314	  if (bc == GKYL_BC_GK_SKIP) {
315	    if (dir == 0)
316	      return ser_gk_collisionless_flux_multib_boundary_surfx_kernels[cv_index[cdim].vdim[vdim]].kernels[poly_order];
317	    else if (dir == 1)
318	      return ser_gk_collisionless_flux_multib_boundary_surfy_kernels[cv_index[cdim].vdim[vdim]].kernels[poly_order];
319	    else if (dir == 2)
320	      return ser_gk_collisionless_flux_multib_boundary_surfz_kernels[cv_index[cdim].vdim[vdim]].kernels[poly_order];
321	    else
322	      return NULL;
323	  }
324	  else {
325	    if (dir == 0)
326	      return ser_gk_collisionless_flux_surfx_kernels[cv_index[cdim].vdim[vdim]].kernels[poly_order];
327	    else if (dir == 1)
328	      return ser_gk_collisionless_flux_surfy_kernels[cv_index[cdim].vdim[vdim]].kernels[poly_order];

0b27cc568 Apply periodicity to potential in 1x field solver (just for the adiabatic test we are using for now), and replace gk_collisionless kernels with fixed ones (gkylcas b31f194ae0295ba71634e2dd9d38be0e7778fcde). I think there'sstill an issue because the field becomes NaNs.
dfd2b503e Change GK collisionless solver so it admits a discontinuous phi and thus a discontinuous Hamiltonian. We compute the gradient of the Yushmanov potential weakly, with a surface term that uses a LF-flux form with a pernalty term that has the opposite sign as the penalty term in the streaming term flux. The hope is this will remove subsonic instabilities. Note that the implementation is horribly memory-inefficient at the moment (the Yushmanov gradient is stored as cdim phase-space arrays). I don't think it's working correctly yet either (gkylcas 9e5fa993822f2e42906bdd2eb30925d9c05ce459).
e55969e03 Use a precomputed ratio of the Jacobians at interblock boundaries. This ratio is unity at parallel boundaries, and we checked that doing it this way is equivalent to multiplication at nodes. Single and multiblock continue to conserve particles, but this way of doing it is more consistent (gkylcas 925653a3811bb6119fe6c667e30ad5c3457c5c2f).

#include <assert.h>

#include <gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_priv.h>
#include <gkyl_util.h>

gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux*
gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_new(const struct gkyl_rect_grid *phase_grid, 
  const struct gkyl_basis *conf_basis, const struct gkyl_basis *phase_basis, 
  const double charge, const double mass,
  enum gkyl_gk_collisionless_type type,
  const struct gk_geometry *gk_geom, const struct gkyl_dg_geom *dg_geom, 
  const struct gkyl_gk_dg_geom *gk_dg_geom, const struct gkyl_velocity_map *vel_map,
  const enum gkyl_gyrokinetic_bc_type *bctype_conf, bool use_gpu)
{
#ifdef GKYL_HAVE_CUDA
  if (use_gpu)
    return gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_cu_dev_new(phase_grid, conf_basis, phase_basis,
      charge, mass, type, gk_geom, dg_geom, gk_dg_geom, vel_map, bctype_conf);
#endif     

  gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux *up = gkyl_malloc(sizeof(gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux));

  up->phase_grid = *phase_grid;
  int cdim = conf_basis->ndim;
  int pdim = phase_basis->ndim;
  int vdim = pdim - cdim;
  int poly_order = phase_basis->poly_order;
  up->cdim = cdim;
  up->pdim = pdim;

  up->charge = charge;
  up->mass = mass;

  up->gk_geom = gkyl_gk_geometry_acquire(gk_geom);
  up->dg_geom = gkyl_dg_geom_acquire(dg_geom);
  up->gk_dg_geom = gkyl_gk_dg_geom_acquire(gk_dg_geom);
  up->vel_map = gkyl_velocity_map_acquire(vel_map);

  if (type == GKYL_GK_COLLISIONLESS_ES) {
    for (int d=0; d<cdim; ++d) {
      // BC option in ->flux_surf kernel doesn't matter as long as it's not SKIP.
      up->flux_surf[d] = choose_gk_collisionless_flux_surf_conf_kern(d, cdim, vdim, poly_order, GKYL_BC_GK_SPECIES_ABSORB);
      up->flux_surf_edge_lo[d] = choose_gk_collisionless_flux_surf_conf_kern(d, cdim, vdim,
        poly_order, bctype_conf[d]);
      up->flux_surf_edge_up[d] = choose_gk_collisionless_flux_edge_surf_conf_kern(d, cdim, vdim,
        poly_order, bctype_conf[GKYL_MAX_CDIM+d]);
    }
    up->flux_surfvpar[0] = choose_gk_collisionless_flux_surf_vpar_kern(cdim, vdim, poly_order);
  }
  else if (type == GKYL_GK_COLLISIONLESS_ES_NO_BY) {
    for (int d=0; d<cdim; ++d) {
      // BC option in ->flux_surf kernel doesn't matter as long as it's not SKIP.
      up->flux_surf[d] = choose_gk_collisionless_flux_no_by_surf_conf_kern(d, cdim, vdim, poly_order, GKYL_BC_GK_SPECIES_ABSORB);
      up->flux_surf_edge_lo[d] = choose_gk_collisionless_flux_no_by_surf_conf_kern(d, cdim, vdim,
        poly_order, bctype_conf[d]);
      up->flux_surf_edge_up[d] = choose_gk_collisionless_flux_no_by_edge_surf_conf_kern(d, cdim, vdim,
        poly_order, bctype_conf[GKYL_MAX_CDIM+d]);
    }
    up->flux_surfvpar[0] = choose_gk_collisionless_flux_no_by_surf_vpar_kern(cdim, vdim, poly_order);
  }

  up->flags = 0;
  GKYL_CLEAR_CU_ALLOC(up->flags);
  up->on_dev = up; // self-reference on host
  
  return up;
}

void gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_surf(struct gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux *up, 
  const struct gkyl_range *conf_range, const struct gkyl_range *phase_range,
  const struct gkyl_range *conf_ext_range, const struct gkyl_range *phase_ext_range, const struct gkyl_array *phi, 
  const struct gkyl_array *fin, struct gkyl_array *yfield, struct gkyl_array* flux_surf, struct gkyl_array *cflrate)
{
#ifdef GKYL_HAVE_CUDA
  if (gkyl_array_is_cu_dev(flux_surf)) {
    return gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_surf_cu(up, conf_range, phase_range,
      conf_ext_range, phase_ext_range, phi, fin, flux_surf, cflrate);
  }
#endif
  int pdim = up->pdim;
  int cdim = up->cdim;
  int idx[GKYL_MAX_DIM], idx_edge[GKYL_MAX_DIM], idx_vel[2];
  int idxL[GKYL_MAX_DIM];
  int idx_velL[2];
  double xc[GKYL_MAX_DIM];

  struct gkyl_range vpar_range;
  int extend_lo[GKYL_MAX_DIM] = {0};
  int extend_up[GKYL_MAX_DIM] = {0};
  extend_lo[cdim] = -1;
  gkyl_range_extend(&vpar_range, phase_range, extend_lo, extend_up);

  gkyl_array_clear(yfield, 0.0);

  struct gkyl_range_iter iter;
  gkyl_range_iter_init(&iter, phase_range);
  while (gkyl_range_iter_next(&iter)) {
    gkyl_copy_int_arr(pdim, iter.idx, idx);

    for (int d=cdim; d<pdim; d++) idx_vel[d-cdim] = iter.idx[d];

    long loc_conf = gkyl_range_idx(conf_range, idx);
    long loc_vel = gkyl_range_idx(&up->vel_map->local_vel, idx_vel);
    long loc_phase = gkyl_range_idx(phase_range, idx);

    gkyl_rect_grid_cell_center(&up->phase_grid, idx, xc);

    const double *bmag_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->gk_geom->geo_corn.bmag, loc_conf);
    const double *vmap_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->vel_map->vmap, loc_vel);
    const double *vmapSq_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->vel_map->vmap_sq, loc_vel);

    double *flux_surf_d = gkyl_array_fetch(flux_surf, loc_phase);
    double *cflrate_d = gkyl_array_fetch(cflrate, loc_phase);

    for (int dir = 0; dir<cdim; ++dir) {
      gkyl_copy_int_arr(pdim, idx, idxL);
      idxL[dir] = idx[dir] - 1;
      long loc_confL = gkyl_range_idx(conf_range, idxL);
      long locL = gkyl_range_idx(phase_range, idxL);
      const double *fL = gkyl_array_cfetch(fin, locL);
      const double *fR = gkyl_array_cfetch(fin, loc_phase);

      const struct gkyl_dg_surf_geom *dgs = gkyl_dg_geom_get_surf(up->dg_geom, dir, idx);
      const struct gkyl_gk_dg_surf_geom *gkdgs = gkyl_gk_dg_geom_get_surf(up->gk_dg_geom, dir, idx);

      const double *jacgeo_rat_surfL_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->gk_geom->geo_surf[dir].jacobgeo_ratio, loc_confL);
      const double *jacgeo_rat_surfR_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->gk_geom->geo_surf[dir].jacobgeo_ratio, loc_conf);

      const double *phiL_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(phi, loc_confL);
      const double *phiR_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(phi, loc_conf);

      double *yfieldL = gkyl_array_fetch(yfield, locL);
      double *yfieldR = gkyl_array_fetch(yfield, loc_phase);

      if (idx[dir] == phase_range->lower[dir]) {
        // Lower domain/block boundary.
        cflrate_d[0] += up->flux_surf_edge_lo[dir](xc, up->phase_grid.dx, vmap_d, vmapSq_d, up->charge, up->mass,
          dgs, gkdgs, bmag_d, jacgeo_rat_surfL_d, jacgeo_rat_surfR_d, phiL_d, phiR_d, fL, fR, yfieldL, yfieldR, flux_surf_d);
      } else {
        // Interior, lower cell surface.
        cflrate_d[0] += up->flux_surf[dir](xc, up->phase_grid.dx, vmap_d, vmapSq_d, up->charge, up->mass,
          dgs, gkdgs, bmag_d, jacgeo_rat_surfL_d, jacgeo_rat_surfR_d, phiL_d, phiR_d, fL, fR, yfieldL, yfieldR, flux_surf_d);
      }

      // Upper domain/block boundary.
      // If the phase space index is at the local configuration space upper value, we
      // we are at the configuration space upper edge and we also need to evaluate 
      // alpha = +1 to avoid evaluating the geometry information in the ghost cells 
      // where it is not defined when computing the final surface alpha we need
      // (since the surface alpha array stores only the *lower* surface expansion)
      if (idx[dir] == phase_range->upper[dir]) {
        gkyl_copy_int_arr(pdim, idx, idx_edge);
        idx_edge[dir] = idx_edge[dir]+1;
        long loc_conf_ext = gkyl_range_idx(conf_ext_range, idx_edge);
        long loc_phase_ext = gkyl_range_idx(phase_ext_range, idx_edge);

        double *cflrate_ext_d = gkyl_array_fetch(cflrate, loc_phase_ext);

        const double *fL = gkyl_array_cfetch(fin, loc_phase);
        const double *fR = gkyl_array_cfetch(fin, loc_phase_ext);

        const struct gkyl_dg_surf_geom *dgs = gkyl_dg_geom_get_surf(up->dg_geom, dir, idx_edge);
        const struct gkyl_gk_dg_surf_geom *gkdgs = gkyl_gk_dg_geom_get_surf(up->gk_dg_geom, dir, idx_edge);

        const double *jacgeo_rat_surfL_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->gk_geom->geo_surf[dir].jacobgeo_ratio, loc_conf);
        const double *jacgeo_rat_surfR_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->gk_geom->geo_surf[dir].jacobgeo_ratio, loc_conf_ext);

        const double *phiL_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(phi, loc_conf);
        const double *phiR_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(phi, loc_conf_ext);

        double *yfieldL = gkyl_array_fetch(yfield, loc_phase);
        double *yfieldR = gkyl_array_fetch(yfield, loc_phase_ext);

        double* flux_surf_ext_d = gkyl_array_fetch(flux_surf, loc_phase_ext);

        cflrate_ext_d[0] += up->flux_surf_edge_up[dir](xc, up->phase_grid.dx, vmap_d, vmapSq_d, up->charge, up->mass,
          dgs, gkdgs, bmag_d, jacgeo_rat_surfL_d, jacgeo_rat_surfR_d, phiL_d, phiR_d, fL, fR, yfieldL, yfieldR, flux_surf_ext_d);
      }  
    }
  }

  gkyl_range_iter_init(&iter, &vpar_range);
  while (gkyl_range_iter_next(&iter)) {
    gkyl_copy_int_arr(pdim, iter.idx, idx);

    for (int d=cdim; d<pdim; d++) idx_vel[d-cdim] = iter.idx[d];

    long loc_conf = gkyl_range_idx(conf_range, idx);
    long loc_vel = gkyl_range_idx(&up->vel_map->local_vel, idx_vel);
    long loc_phase = gkyl_range_idx(phase_range, idx);

    gkyl_rect_grid_cell_center(&up->phase_grid, idx, xc);

    const double *bmag_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->gk_geom->geo_corn.bmag, loc_conf);
    const double *vmap_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->vel_map->vmap, loc_vel);
    const double *vmapSq_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->vel_map->vmap_sq, loc_vel);
    const double *yfield_d = gkyl_array_cfetch(yfield, loc_phase);

    double *flux_surf_d = gkyl_array_fetch(flux_surf, loc_phase);
    double *cflrate_d = gkyl_array_fetch(cflrate, loc_phase);

    int dir=cdim;
    gkyl_copy_int_arr(pdim, idx, idxL);
    idxL[dir] = idx[dir] - 1;
    gkyl_copy_int_arr(pdim-cdim, idx_vel, idx_velL);
    idx_velL[0] = idx_velL[0]-1;
    long locL = gkyl_range_idx(phase_range, idxL);
    long loc_velL = gkyl_range_idx(&up->vel_map->local_vel, idx_velL);
    const double *fL = gkyl_array_cfetch(fin, locL);
    const double *fR = gkyl_array_cfetch(fin, loc_phase);

    const double *vpL = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->vel_map->vmap_prime, loc_velL);
    const double *vpR = gkyl_array_cfetch(up->vel_map->vmap_prime, loc_vel);

    const struct gkyl_dg_vol_geom *dgv = gkyl_dg_geom_get_vol(up->dg_geom, idx);
    const struct gkyl_gk_dg_vol_geom *gkdgv = gkyl_gk_dg_geom_get_vol(up->gk_dg_geom, idx);
    cflrate_d[0] += up->flux_surfvpar[0](xc, up->phase_grid.dx, vpL, vpR, vmap_d, vmapSq_d, up->charge, up->mass,
      dgv, gkdgv, bmag_d, yfield_d, fL, fR, flux_surf_d);
  }
}

void gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_release(gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux *up)
{
  gkyl_gk_geometry_release(up->gk_geom);
  gkyl_dg_geom_release(up->dg_geom);
  gkyl_gk_dg_geom_release(up->gk_dg_geom);
  gkyl_velocity_map_release(up->vel_map);
  
  if (GKYL_IS_CU_ALLOC(up->flags))
    gkyl_cu_free(up->on_dev);
  gkyl_free(up);
}

- `gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_{lower,upper}_multib_...` (multiblock/SKIP boundary — just lower/upper, no periodic/nonperiodic split)

That resolves my open question entirely — multib only needs lower/upper, no periodicity distinction to invent. Good, no new plumbing needed there. Let me discard my earlier incorrect assumption and re-verify the actual kernel bodies quickly before finalizing the plan design.

Confirmed exactly as you said — the multib file has only `lower`/`upper` variants, no periodic/nonperiodic split (uses `JfL`/`JfR` set to `0.0` on the missing side since there's no valid neighbor block data). Good, that fully resolves my open question — no new periodicity plumbing needed anywhere. I now have everything needed to design the plan. Let me check the periodic/nonperiodic (non-multib) files and the current `gk_collisionless_flux.c`/priv.h state once more, then write the plan.

# Add lower/upper boundary special cases to GK collisionless flux updater

## Context

`gyrokinetic/zero/gk_collisionless_flux.c` computes the DG collisionless
gyrokinetic flux at phase-space cell surfaces. For each configuration
direction `dir`, every cell currently does one of two things at its own
*lower* face: if `idx[dir] == phase_range->lower[dir]` it calls
`flux_surf_edge_lo[dir]`, otherwise it calls the plain interior kernel
`flux_surf[dir]`. Separately, the last interior cell
(`idx[dir] == phase_range->upper[dir]`) also evaluates an *extra* face
beyond itself (the domain/block upper edge) using `flux_surf_edge_up[dir]`.

The catch: today `flux_surf_edge_lo[dir]` is chosen via
`choose_gk_collisionless_flux_surf_conf_kern()`, the *same* chooser used for
the interior kernel — it only diverges from the interior kernel when the BC
is `GKYL_BC_GK_SKIP` (multiblock). So at a periodic or physical
(non-multiblock) lower boundary, the "lower boundary" face is today
evaluated with the *ordinary interior* kernel — there is no dedicated
lower-boundary kernel, unlike the upper boundary which always uses a
dedicated edge kernel regardless of BC type.

The user has written new Maxima-generated kernels that fix this asymmetry:
for the 1x2v/p1/x-direction case there are now three dedicated kernel
*pairs*, each split into `_lower_` and `_upper_` variants:

- `gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_{lower,upper}_periodic_1x2v_ser_p1`
- `gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_{lower,upper}_nonperiodic_1x2v_ser_p1`
- `gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_{lower,upper}_multib_1x2v_ser_p1`

(`gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_multib_1x2v_ser_p1.c`,
`..._nonperiodic_1x2v_ser_p1.c`, `..._periodic_1x2v_ser_p1.c`, all in
`gyrokinetic/ker/gk_collisionless_flux/`, declared in
`gyrokinetic/ker/gk_collisionless_flux/gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_kernels.h`).
The regenerated kernel header now declares this naming scheme for *all*
dims/poly-orders/directions/no_by variants, but only the 1x2v/p1/x-dir `.c`
bodies exist so far — the rest will be filled in later. Critically, the
regenerated header **no longer declares the old kernel names**
(`gk_collisionless_flux_edge_surfx_*`, `gk_collisionless_flux_multib_boundary_surfx_*`,
`gk_collisionless_flux_multib_boundary_edge_surfx_*`) at all, for any dim —
so `gyrokinetic/zero/gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_priv.h`, which still
references those old names, is presently broken and must be rewritten
against the new scheme.

Goal: restructure `gk_collisionless_flux.c`'s per-direction loop so lower
and upper domain/block boundaries are both clean, dedicated special cases
(each backed by its own genuinely-boundary-specific kernel), and rewrite
`gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_priv.h` to dispatch to the new
lower/upper × periodic/nonperiodic/multib kernel set. **Host (C) code only**
— `gk_collisionless_flux_cu.cu` (the CUDA path) is explicitly out of scope
and will be updated in a follow-up once the C version is finalized.

## Kernel semantics (verified from the 1x2v/p1/x-dir kernels)

- `_lower_*` kernels: build `hamil` from `phiR` (the current/owning cell),
  treat the current cell as R and its `idx-1` neighbor as L, and (except
  for multib) add the `ypotderR[...]` correction terms. This is exactly the
  shape of the plain interior kernel, but is a **separate, boundary-aware**
  kernel now.
- `_upper_*` kernels: build `hamil` from `phiL` (the current/owning cell is
  L), evaluate the extra ghost/edge face beyond the last interior cell, and
  have no `ypotderR` correction terms.
- `periodic`: both `JfL_quad`/`JfR_quad` and `ypotL_quad`/`ypotR_quad` are
  genuinely two-sided (periodic wraparound gives valid neighbor data).
- `nonperiodic`: two-sided `Jf*_quad`, but `ypotL_quad`/`ypotR_quad` are
  both computed from the *owning* cell's `phi` only (one-sided — the
  physical boundary's ghost `phi` isn't trusted).
- `multib`: the non-owning side's `Jf*_quad` is hardcoded to `0.0` at every
  quadrature point (`JfL_quad=0` for lower, `JfR_quad=0` for upper) since
  the neighbor block's `f`/`Jf` isn't validly synced; no periodic/
  nonperiodic split exists for multib — only lower/upper.

`GKYL_BC_GK_SKIP` (== multib) is already available at construction time via
`bctype_conf`, as is `GKYL_BC_GK_SPECIES_PERIODIC`/`GKYL_BC_GK_FIELD_PERIODIC`
— no new plumbing/parameters are needed to distinguish the three cases.

## Implementation

### 1. `gyrokinetic/zero/gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_priv.h`

- Keep `struct gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux` fields unchanged
  (`flux_surf`, `flux_surf_edge_lo`, `flux_surf_edge_up`, `flux_surfvpar`) —
  no renaming, since `gk_collisionless_flux_cu.cu` (untouched) references
  these field names.
- Replace the old kernel-list tables
  `ser_gk_collisionless_flux_edge_surf{x,y,z}_kernels`,
  `ser_gk_collisionless_flux_multib_boundary_surf{x,y,z}_kernels`,
  `ser_gk_collisionless_flux_multib_boundary_edge_surf{x,y,z}_kernels`
  (and their `no_by` counterparts) with six new tables per direction,
  mirroring the new naming scheme, e.g. for x:
  - `ser_gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_lower_periodic_kernels`
  - `ser_gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_upper_periodic_kernels`
  - `ser_gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_lower_nonperiodic_kernels`
  - `ser_gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_upper_nonperiodic_kernels`
  - `ser_gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_lower_multib_kernels`
  - `ser_gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_upper_multib_kernels`
  (same set for `surfy`/`surfz`, and again with `_no_by_` inserted for the
  `GKYL_GK_COLLISIONLESS_ES_NO_BY` variant — 36 tables total). Only fill in
  entries that have a real kernel today (1x2v/p1/x-dir); everything else is
  `NULL`, matching the existing convention for not-yet-generated combos.
- Replace `choose_gk_collisionless_flux_edge_surf_conf_kern` and
  `choose_gk_collisionless_flux_no_by_edge_surf_conf_kern` with two pairs of
  new choosers (regular + no_by), one for the lower boundary and one for
  the upper boundary, e.g.:
  ```c
  static gk_collisionless_flux_surf_t
  choose_gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_lo_conf_kern(int dir, int cdim, int vdim,
    int poly_order, enum gkyl_gyrokinetic_bc_type bc)
  {
    if (bc == GKYL_BC_GK_SKIP)
      return /* ser_..._boundary_surf{x,y,z}_lower_multib_kernels[...] by dir */;
    else if (bc == GKYL_BC_GK_SPECIES_PERIODIC || bc == GKYL_BC_GK_FIELD_PERIODIC)
      return /* ..._lower_periodic_kernels[...] by dir */;
    else
      return /* ..._lower_nonperiodic_kernels[...] by dir */;
  }
  ```
  and the `_up_` counterpart using the `upper_*` tables. Plus `_no_by_`
  versions of both.
- Simplify `choose_gk_collisionless_flux_surf_conf_kern` (and its `no_by`
  counterpart), which is used only for the interior `flux_surf[d]` kernel:
  drop the `bc == GKYL_BC_GK_SKIP` branch (the multib table it pointed to
  is being removed, and interior cells are never at a multiblock boundary)
  — always look up the plain interior table. Keep the function's signature
  (including the now-unused `bc` parameter) unchanged so
  `gk_collisionless_flux_cu.cu`'s existing call sites keep compiling.

Note: with these table/chooser removals, `gk_collisionless_flux_cu.cu`'s
calls to `choose_gk_collisionless_flux_edge_surf_conf_kern` /
`choose_gk_collisionless_flux_no_by_edge_surf_conf_kern` will no longer
resolve. That file is intentionally left untouched per the user's request
and will be fixed in the follow-up CUDA pass; this only matters when
`GKYL_HAVE_CUDA` is enabled.

### 2. `gyrokinetic/zero/gk_collisionless_flux.c`

In `gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_new()`, change the `flux_surf_edge_lo`/
`flux_surf_edge_up` assignments (in both the `GKYL_GK_COLLISIONLESS_ES` and
`GKYL_GK_COLLISIONLESS_ES_NO_BY` branches) to use the new lower/upper
choosers instead of `choose_gk_collisionless_flux_surf_conf_kern` /
`choose_gk_collisionless_flux_edge_surf_conf_kern`:
```c
up->flux_surf_edge_lo[d] = choose_gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_lo_conf_kern(d, cdim, vdim,
  poly_order, bctype_conf[d]);
up->flux_surf_edge_up[d] = choose_gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_up_conf_kern(d, cdim, vdim,
  poly_order, bctype_conf[GKYL_MAX_CDIM+d]);
```
(and the `_no_by_` variants in the other branch). `flux_surf[d]`'s
assignment is unchanged.

In `gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_surf()`, restructure the `for (int dir = 0;
dir < cdim; ++dir)` loop so the three cases read as clear, clearly-labeled
special cases instead of an if/else followed by a bolted-on extra `if`:
```c
for (int dir = 0; dir < cdim; ++dir) {
  ... (unchanged: idxL, loc_confL, locL, fL, fR, dgs, gkdgs, jacgeo_rat_surf{L,R}_d,
       phi{L,R}_d, yfield{L,R} setup for this cell's own lower face) ...

  if (idx[dir] == phase_range->lower[dir]) {
    // Lower domain/block boundary: this cell's own lower face is the
    // domain/block boundary face.
    cflrate_d[0] += up->flux_surf_edge_lo[dir](...);
  } else {
    // Interior lower face.
    cflrate_d[0] += up->flux_surf[dir](...);
  }

  if (idx[dir] == phase_range->upper[dir]) {
    // Upper domain/block boundary: an *extra* face beyond this (last
    // interior) cell, into the ghost/ext range.
    ... (unchanged: idx_edge, loc_conf_ext, loc_phase_ext, fL/fR, dgs, gkdgs,
         jacgeo_rat_surf{L,R}_d, phi{L,R}_d, yfield{L,R}, flux_surf_ext_d) ...
    cflrate_ext_d[0] += up->flux_surf_edge_up[dir](...);
  }
}
```
This keeps the existing (and necessary) two-part shape — a cell's own
lower face is either interior or a lower boundary; independently, the last
cell also owns an extra upper-boundary face beyond it — but makes both
boundary cases explicit, comment-labeled special cases wired to their own
dedicated kernels, symmetric with each other. No change to the vpar loop
or the second half of the function.

## Verification

Since only 1x2v/p1/x-direction kernels exist, meaningful runtime testing is
limited to that configuration:
- Build the gyrokinetic host target and confirm it compiles with
  `GKYL_HAVE_CUDA` unset (default on this machine).
- Run/inspect `gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_detach_1d.c` or another 1x2v regression
  test that exercises this updater, and confirm results are unchanged for
  periodic BCs (should numerically match pre-change behavior since the new
  `_lower_periodic_1x2v_ser_p1` kernel should be equivalent to the old
  reused-interior-kernel behavior for a periodic lower face).
- Grep the build output / compile log for any remaining references to the
  old kernel names (`gk_collisionless_flux_edge_surfx`,
  `gk_collisionless_flux_multib_boundary_surfx`,
  `gk_collisionless_flux_multib_boundary_edge_surfx`) to confirm the
  rewrite is complete on the host side.

## Context

`gyrokinetic/zero/gk_collisionless_flux.c` computes the DG collisionless
gyrokinetic flux at phase-space cell surfaces. For each configuration
direction `dir`, every cell currently does one of two things at its own
*lower* face: if `idx[dir] == phase_range->lower[dir]` it calls
`flux_surf_edge_lo[dir]`, otherwise it calls the plain interior kernel
`flux_surf[dir]`. Separately, the last interior cell
(`idx[dir] == phase_range->upper[dir]`) also evaluates an *extra* face
beyond itself (the domain/block upper edge) using `flux_surf_edge_up[dir]`.

The catch: today `flux_surf_edge_lo[dir]` is chosen via
`choose_gk_collisionless_flux_surf_conf_kern()`, the *same* chooser used for
the interior kernel — it only diverges from the interior kernel when the BC
is `GKYL_BC_GK_SKIP` (multiblock). So at a periodic or physical
(non-multiblock) lower boundary, the "lower boundary" face is today
evaluated with the *ordinary interior* kernel — there is no dedicated
lower-boundary kernel, unlike the upper boundary which always uses a
dedicated edge kernel regardless of BC type.

The user has written new Maxima-generated kernels that fix this asymmetry:
for the 1x2v/p1/x-direction case there are now three dedicated kernel
*pairs*, each split into `_lower_` and `_upper_` variants:

- `gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_{lower,upper}_periodic_1x2v_ser_p1`
- `gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_{lower,upper}_nonperiodic_1x2v_ser_p1`
- `gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfx_{lower,upper}_multib_1x2v_ser_p1`

`..._nonperiodic_1x2v_ser_p1.c`, `..._periodic_1x2v_ser_p1.c`, all in

`gyrokinetic/ker/gk_collisionless_flux/gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_kernels.h`).

dims/poly-orders/directions/no_by variants, but only the 1x2v/p1/x-dir `.c`
bodies exist so far — the rest will be filled in later. Critically, the
regenerated header **no longer declares the old kernel names**

    core_tokens = set(core.split('_'))
    rows = re.findall(r'\{([^{}]*)\}', body)
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        cols = [c.strip() for c in row.split(',')]
        for ci, c in enumerate(cols):
            if c == 'NULL':

            if ci != 1:

            kern_core = c.replace("gk_collisionless_flux_", "")
            kern_core = re.sub(r'_ser_p\d$', '', kern_core)
            kern_core = re.sub(r'_(1x1v|1x2v|2x2v|3x2v)$', '', kern_core)
            kern_tokens = set(kern_core.split('_'))
            if kern_tokens != core_tokens:
                issues.append((name, i, "token mismatch", c, sorted(core_tokens), sorted(kern_tokens)))
            expected_dim = dim_for_row[i]
            if expected_dim not in c:
                issues.append((name, i, "dim mismatch", c, expected_dim))

print(f"Total issues: {len(issues)}")
for it in issues:

EOF

Everything's in order now. Summary of the audit:

**What was checked:**
- All 90 kernel functions referenced in `gyrokinetic/zero/gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_priv.h` are declared in `gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_kernels.h` and have real `.c` definitions (no dangling references, no missing kernels).
- All 44 dispatch tables (interior surfx/y/z/vpar + `no_by` variants, plus 36 boundary tables across lower/upper × periodic/nonperiodic/multib × x/y/z) have exactly the required 4 rows matching the `cv_index[cdim].vdim[vdim]` indexing convention (row 0=1x1v, 1=1x2v, 2=2x2v, 3=3x2v), with each kernel sitting in the correct row (dimensionality) and column (poly_order=1).
- The choosers (`choose_gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_conf_kern`, its `no_by` counterpart, and the interior/vpar choosers) correctly dispatch to these tables by direction, edge, and BC type.

**Bug found and fixed:** my own earlier edit had mis-populated the 18 non-`no_by` boundary tables — merging 1x1v/1x2v into one row and shifting 2x2v/3x2v up, which would have caused wrong-kernel dispatch (or misalignment) for boundary cells in every dimensionality except the one that happened to still line up. Rewrote all 18 tables with the correct 4-row layout, then populated the previously-all-NULL 18 `no_by` boundary tables the same way, using the confirmed-existing 2x2v/3x2v (z: 3x2v only) `no_by` boundary kernels.

**Verification:** rebuilt `gyrokinetic` host target clean (zero errors/warnings), rebuilt and ran `rt_gk_sheath_1x2v_p1` to completion (100%, no NaN/inf/crash — the RK stage-2/3 "failures" logged are normal adaptive-timestep retries).

The kernel header you regenerated is confirmed clean; the fix was entirely in `gyrokinetic/zero/gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_priv.h` (uncommitted, working tree only — nothing pushed).
